## 21d822423cfc

**A1 — reproduced production teaching defect.** Version3.0.0; generator SHA-256
`7fc3fefaac4b90e808db17e3b31e5078796a2cd2d9ed00506d2bd3bba7dde595`;
active Racket hash `70caebbaa31c`. The supplied catalog marks this task approved;
that metadata is not a guarantee that each lesson is identifiable.

For seed42, medium, no overrides, accepted indices[0,1,2,3], use the first three
as demonstrations and the last as query. Profiles are `four_seed_ambiguous`,
`open_edge_chambers`, `four_seed_blank`, `multiple_same_seed`. All four pass the
target validator and come directly from its documented generator domain.

Correct behavior fills a chamber with exactly one distinct seed color, including
several seed cells of that same color. The plausible rival fills only a chamber
with exactly one seed cell. It matches all three visible labels but disagrees
on37 query cells. The public production sampler reproduces the exact four inputs
and outputs, with zero rejections, and reports `lesson_check.status=not_declared`.
This is a teaching ambiguity, not an allegation of incorrect Racket labels.

Evidence: `checks/audit/21d822423cfc/probe.json`, `input.json`, `racket.json`,
`production.jsonl`, `verification.json`; exact commands in RESULTS.json and
`checks/audit-a-apply.log`, `checks/audit-a-production.log`.
The bounded discovery search tested seeds0..42 and stopped at the first witness;
this is one counterexample, not an estimated corpus failure rate.

Suggested task-owner repair: declare the rival and a multiple-same-color witness;
ensure a three-demo lesson teaches that distinction whenever the query needs it.
Then check actual production assembly and any permitted holdout rotations.
Do not simply ban legitimate repeated-seed queries or change the distinct-color rule.
